messages.text:
I can't honestly name a single best trading strategy for your portfolio. The backtests didn't cover most of your money, and none of the results are strong enough to rely on. What the data does show clearly is a concentration risk, and that's worth fixing first.

## Your portfolio
Worth **$82,905**, up **51.8%** (+$28,290) on $54,615 invested.

| Holding | Value | Share of portfolio | Gain |
|---|---|---|---|
| NVDA | $27,008 | **32.6%** | +70.8% |
| AAPL | $17,054 | **20.6%** | +71.9% |
| MSFT | $15,485 | 18.7% | +25.3% |
| JPM | $13,722 | 16.6% | +40.3% |
| XOM | $9,635 | 11.6% | +43.0% |

The risk check flagged three problems:
- 🔴 **Critical:** Technology is **71.8%** of the portfolio; the limit is 50%.
- ⚠️ NVDA (32.6%) and AAPL (20.6%) are each over the 20% limit for a single position.

## Backtest results (last 12 months)
I tested six strategies on all five stocks, but **each test only returned results for MSFT and JPM.** AAPL, NVDA and XOM, which make up about 65% of your money, were left out with no explanation. The RSI and Channel Breakout results were too large to load, so I don't have them.

| Strategy | MSFT | JPM | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Momentum** | **+21.8%** (Sharpe 1.16) | −2.8% | Best MSFT result, but only 2 trades |
| MACD | +6.7% (Sharpe 0.54) | JPM missing from results | Modest |
| SMA Crossover | +0.5% (won 1 of 8 trades) | +1.8% | Weak |
| Bollinger Bands | **−17.3%** | +2.4% | Avoid |

**Why I wouldn't act on these:**
- Momentum's MSFT result rests on two trades, one of which gained 28%. That's too few to separate skill from luck.
- JPM went from about $305 to $343 during the test (roughly +12%). All three JPM strategies I have results for made less than that (between −2.8% and +2.4%), so simply holding would have done better.
- The stocks that drive your returns (NVDA, AAPL, XOM) weren't tested at all.

## My suggestion
1. **Deal with concentration before choosing a trading strategy.** If tech falls, it hits almost three-quarters of your portfolio at once. Selling part of NVDA and AAPL, which have both gained about 70%, and moving the money into other sectors (healthcare, consumer staples, industrials) would bring tech closer to 50%. Selling will likely trigger capital gains tax. NVDA was bought 2025-10-21, so it becomes a long-term holding (usually taxed at a lower rate) after 2026-10-21, less than a month away. That's worth waiting for if you plan to sell it.
2. **If you want a rules-based approach, momentum looks most promising.** Before trusting it, I'd test it properly: backtest each stock one at a time (especially NVDA and AAPL), then run a walk-forward test, which checks whether the rules keep working on data they weren't tuned on.
3. **Holding what you have is a reasonable default.** Your stocks have been rising, and most of these trading strategies did worse than just holding them.

Which direction do you want to take: a rebalancing plan with position sizes, or proper backtests of momentum on NVDA, AAPL and XOM?

*This is analysis, not financial advice. Past backtest results don't guarantee future returns.*
